portInfo.description: Hong Kong’s Tourism Commission describes the city as a regional cruise hub with Victoria Harbour (no air-draft limit) and two equipped berthing facilities: Ocean Terminal at Tsim Sha Tsui and Kai Tak Cruise Terminal (opened June 2013) on the former runway tip, sized for the world’s largest cruise vessels. Development parameters for Kai Tak include two berths, an 850 m apron, 12–13 m water depth, nil air draft, 3,000 passengers/hour CIQS capacity, 110,000 displacement / 220,000 GT and 360 m LOA. The HKTB Asia Cruise Hub brochure splits Kai Tak apron lengths as first berth 455 m and second 395 m with five boarding bridges, versus Ocean Terminal South 381 m / North 320 m and draft 10 m. Ocean Terminal’s operator page matches those berth lengths, 10.0 m max draft, 50,000 t max displacement and six telescopic gangways.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Confirm Kai Tak vs Ocean Terminal before assuming a short walk.
